payload.prompt: What is a convolutional neural network (CNN)?

options.text: A deep-learning model that uses filters to extract image features
options.rationale: This is correct because a CNN is a deep-learning architecture. Its filters extract numeric image features used to predict labels.

options.text: A collection of images with known categories
options.rationale: This describes labeled training data rather than a CNN. The collection supplies examples from which a model learns.
options.better_fit: This would be correct when defining training data for supervised learning.

options.text: An image model that processes patches with attention
options.rationale: This describes a vision transformer rather than a CNN. CNNs are distinguished here by their use of filters.
options.better_fit: This would fit a vision transformer architecture.

options.text: A small weighted array applied during filtering
options.rationale: This is a filter kernel, not a complete CNN. A CNN contains filters and later prediction stages.
options.better_fit: This would be correct when naming the weights used by one convolutional filter.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A CNN uses filters to extract image features and predict labels.

payload.prompt: Which statements describe deep learning or CNNs?

options.text: Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers
options.rationale: This is correct because multiple neural-network layers characterize deep learning. Those layers can learn increasingly useful patterns.

options.text: CNN filters extract numeric image features
options.rationale: This is correct because CNN filters produce numeric representations of visual patterns. These features help distinguish image classes.

options.text: A CNN can predict labels for new images
options.rationale: This is correct because the model learns patterns from training examples. It then applies learned patterns to new images.

options.text: A CNN manually assigns known labels to training images
options.rationale: Known labels are prepared for training images rather than manually assigned by the CNN. The model learns by comparing predictions with those labels.
options.better_fit: This would fit the work of a person preparing labeled training data.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Deep learning uses multilayer networks, and CNNs use filters before predicting labels.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: A machine learning model learns patterns from training data to make predictions for new data.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training data provides patterns that support predictions for new data.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Without learned patterns, a new fruit image could not be classified from prior examples.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Machine learning learns from training data and applies learned patterns to new data.

payload.prompt: The training examples used to teach a model patterns are called _____.

parts.text: The training examples used to teach a model patterns are called

payload.explanation: Training data is the collection of existing examples from which a machine learning model learns patterns.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The examples would be confused with either a model or a different architecture.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A CNN is a model that learns from training data; training data is the collection of examples used for learning.

payload.prompt: A grocery-store engineer needs a filter-based deep-learning model that learns from labeled fruit photos and predicts a label for each new camera image. Which model should the engineer choose?

options.text: A convolutional neural network
options.rationale: This is correct because the required model is explicitly filter-based and learns from labeled images. A CNN extracts image features and predicts a fruit label.

options.text: A vision transformer
options.rationale: A vision transformer is an image-model architecture, but it processes patches with attention rather than using the specified filter-based approach. It does not match the engineer's CNN requirement.
options.better_fit: This would fit a decision to use a patch-and-attention image architecture.

feedback.intrinsic: The selected system would not implement the requested filter-based design.
feedback.instructional: Choose a CNN when the design calls for filters that extract image features before label prediction.

options.text: A set of fruit labels
options.rationale: Labels identify known categories but cannot learn visual patterns or classify a new photo. The engineer needs a model that learns from the labeled examples.
options.better_fit: This would fit preparing category names for a training dataset.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout would know category names but have no mechanism to recognize a new fruit image.
feedback.instructional: Labels are training information; a CNN is the model that learns from them and predicts labels.

options.text: A softmax output function
options.rationale: Softmax converts already-produced class scores into probabilities. It does not extract image features or form a complete image-classification model.
options.better_fit: This would fit the final probability-conversion stage after class scores are available.

feedback.intrinsic: The system would have probabilities only if another model had already produced class scores.
feedback.instructional: A CNN includes feature extraction and prediction; softmax is only one later output step.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A CNN uses filters to learn image features and predict labels.

payload.prompt: Which actions are part of CNN feature extraction?

options.text: Filters create numeric feature maps
options.rationale: This is correct because filters create numeric arrays called feature maps. The maps represent extracted visual features.

options.text: Pooling downsizes feature maps
options.rationale: This is correct because pooling reduces the size of feature maps. It can emphasize key visual features.

options.text: Flattening creates one one-dimensional feature array
options.rationale: This is correct because flattening converts feature-map values into one array. That array can be passed to a fully connected network.

options.text: Softmax creates feature maps
options.rationale: Softmax creates class probabilities, not feature maps. Filters create feature maps earlier in the CNN.
options.better_fit: This would fit converting class scores into probabilities.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Filters create maps, pooling can downsize them, and flattening prepares values for the network.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Flattening changes feature maps into a two-dimensional array of feature values.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Flattening creates one one-dimensional array of feature values.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The next neural-network stage would receive the features in the wrong form.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Flattening converts feature maps into a single one-dimensional array.

payload.prompt: Arrange these CNN feature-extraction steps in order.
payload.explanation: Filters create feature maps, pooling can reduce them, and flattening prepares one array for the network.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Values would reach a later stage before their required preparation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the data flow from filters to pooling, then flattening, then the network.

payload.prompt: Arrays of numeric values created by CNN filters are called _____.

parts.text: Arrays of numeric values created by CNN filters are called

payload.explanation: Filters extract visual features as numeric arrays called feature maps.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The filter output would be assigned the name of a different CNN component.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A filter kernel is applied to an image, while the resulting numeric array is a feature map.

payload.prompt: A smart-checkout developer has feature maps from a fruit image and must prepare them for a fully connected network while emphasizing key features. Which actions should the developer choose?

options.text: Pool the feature maps
options.rationale: This is correct because pooling downsizes feature maps and can emphasize key features. It is an appropriate preparation step.

options.text: Flatten the feature maps
options.rationale: This is correct because flattening converts map values into one one-dimensional array. The fully connected network receives flattened values.

options.text: Send flattened values to the network
options.rationale: This is correct because the fully connected network uses flattened feature values as input. Those values support later class scoring.

options.text: Use softmax to create feature maps
options.rationale: Softmax produces class probabilities and cannot create feature maps. Feature maps must already be produced by filters.
options.better_fit: This would fit converting class scores to probabilities after the network has produced scores.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would skip the actual feature-processing path needed by the network.
feedback.instructional: Use pooling and flattening to prepare filter outputs. Reserve softmax for the final probability stage.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Pooling and flattening prepare extracted features for the fully connected network.

payload.prompt: What does softmax produce for image classes?

options.text: One probability for each possible class
options.rationale: This is correct because softmax converts class scores into probabilities. Each possible class receives one probability value.

options.text: One filter kernel for each image
options.rationale: Filter kernels are weighted arrays used during feature extraction. Softmax instead acts on class scores at the output stage.
options.better_fit: This would fit discussing weights used by convolutional filters.

options.text: One known label for each training image
options.rationale: Known labels are supplied with training images. Softmax produces predicted probabilities rather than known labels.
options.better_fit: This would fit describing labeled training data.

options.text: One loss value for each pixel
options.rationale: Loss measures prediction difference from actual labels, whereas softmax produces class probabilities. It is not a pixel-level loss calculation.
options.better_fit: This would fit neither stage; loss is calculated from predictions and actual labels.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Softmax converts class scores into a probability for every possible class.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: A fully connected neural network receives flattened feature values and produces class scores.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Flattened features enter the fully connected network, which produces class scores.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The path from image features to class probabilities would be placed in the wrong order.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Flattened values enter the fully connected network before softmax converts its class scores into probabilities.

payload.prompt: The function that converts class scores into probabilities is _____.

parts.text: The function that converts class scores into probabilities is

payload.explanation: Softmax converts class scores into a probability for each class.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The class scores would not be converted into probability values.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Pooling and flattening prepare features, while loss measures error. Softmax produces class probabilities.

payload.prompt: Arrange the path from flattened features to class probabilities.
payload.explanation: Flattened values enter the fully connected network, which produces scores before softmax gives probabilities.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The probability result would appear before the values needed to produce it.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The correct sequence is network input, class scores, then softmax probabilities.

payload.prompt: A checkout system maps positions 0, 1, and 2 to apple, banana, and orange. Its softmax output is [0.2, 0.5, 0.3], and the cashier must choose one label. Which decision is correct?

options.text: Select the class at position 1
options.rationale: This is correct because position 1 has the highest probability, 0.5. The mapping identifies position 1 as banana.

options.text: Select the class at position 0
options.rationale: Position 0 has probability 0.2, which is not the highest output value. It corresponds to apple, not the strongest prediction.
options.better_fit: This would fit if position 0 had the largest probability.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout could record a lower-confidence fruit category.
feedback.instructional: When one label is required, select the class associated with the largest softmax probability.

options.text: Select the class at position 2
options.rationale: Position 2 has probability 0.3, below the 0.5 at position 1. It corresponds to orange, not the strongest prediction.
options.better_fit: This would fit if position 2 had the largest probability.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout could choose orange despite the stronger middle-position prediction.
feedback.instructional: Compare all softmax values and select the largest one; here that is position 1.

options.text: Select every class because each has a probability
options.rationale: The output contains a probability for every possible class, but the task requires one predicted label. The highest-probability class should be selected.
options.better_fit: This would fit reporting the full probability distribution rather than making one classification decision.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout would not settle on a single fruit category.
feedback.instructional: Use the probability distribution to choose one label by taking its largest value.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The highest probability is at position 1, which maps to banana.

payload.prompt: Which items can be training data for a fruit CNN?

options.text: An apple image labeled apple
options.rationale: This is correct because it pairs an existing image with its known category. That pairing is a labeled training example.

options.text: A banana image labeled banana
options.rationale: This is correct because it is an existing image paired with a known label. The model can learn from this example.

options.text: An orange image labeled orange
options.rationale: This is correct because the image has its actual known category. It can be used in supervised training.

options.text: A new image with no known label
options.error_type: Confuses prediction data with training data
options.rationale: An unlabeled new image lacks the actual category needed for training comparison. It is suitable for prediction after training.
options.better_fit: This would fit an image the trained CNN is asked to classify.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training data contains existing images paired with known labels.

payload.prompt: What is a label in a fruit image model?

options.text: A text category for an image
options.rationale: This is correct because a label names an image category, such as apple or banana. It can be known during training or predicted later.

options.text: A numeric filter weight
options.rationale: Weights are adjustable numeric parameters in filters and networks. A label names the image category instead.
options.better_fit: This would fit a parameter changed during training.

options.text: A probability for a possible class
options.rationale: A probability expresses the model's confidence in a possible class. A label is the category name itself.
options.better_fit: This would fit a softmax output value.

options.text: A numeric feature map
options.rationale: A feature map is a numeric array created by CNN filters. A label is a category name, not extracted visual data.
options.better_fit: This would fit the numeric output of a CNN filter.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A label names an image category.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: Training data for a fruit CNN consists of new images whose labels are unknown.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training data uses existing images with known labels.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model could predict, but it could not compare its prediction with the actual fruit category.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Training examples require known labels; unknown-label images are used for later predictions.

payload.prompt: Arrange these training-preparation steps in order.
payload.explanation: Images need known labels before the network can learn from the examples.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The network would be asked to learn before it had labeled examples.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Collect images first, label them, feed them to the network, and then let the network learn.

payload.prompt: A grocery-store technician is preparing fruit photos so a new CNN can learn. Which choices should the technician make?

options.text: Pair apple photos with the label apple
options.rationale: This is correct because the label identifies the actual category of each apple photo. It creates usable supervised training examples.

options.text: Pair banana photos with the label banana
options.rationale: This is correct because known labels let the CNN compare predictions with actual categories. Banana photos become labeled training examples.

options.text: Pair orange photos with the label orange
options.rationale: This is correct because every orange photo receives its known category. The labeled pairs support learning.

options.text: Keep every fruit photo unlabeled
options.error_type: Uses unlabeled data for supervised training
options.rationale: Unlabeled photos do not provide actual categories for comparison during supervised training. The CNN needs known labels to learn from these examples.
options.better_fit: This would fit collecting new images for a trained CNN to classify.

feedback.intrinsic: The technician could not determine whether the training predictions matched the actual fruits.
feedback.instructional: Pair each training photo with its known category so predictions can be compared with actual labels.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Known labels turn the fruit photos into supervised training data.

payload.prompt: For apple 0, banana 1, and orange 2, which description identifies the banana target output?

options.text: It has 1.0 in the middle position and 0.0 elsewhere
options.rationale: This is correct because banana is class 1, the middle position. A target places 1.0 at the known class position.

options.text: It has 1.0 in the first position and 0.0 elsewhere
options.rationale: The first position represents class 0, apple. It would mark the image as apple rather than banana.
options.better_fit: This would fit an apple image target.

options.text: It has 1.0 in the final position and 0.0 elsewhere
options.rationale: The final position represents class 2, orange. It would mark the image as orange rather than banana.
options.better_fit: This would fit an orange image target.

options.text: It gives nonzero probabilities to all three classes
options.rationale: A probability distribution is a model prediction rather than the known target. A known banana target uses 1.0 only at banana's class position.
options.better_fit: This would fit a softmax prediction over three classes.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Banana is class 1, so its target has 1.0 in the middle position.

payload.prompt: Which statements about image classes and target outputs are correct?

options.text: A class is a possible category
options.rationale: This is correct because a class is one possible category the model can predict. Apple, banana, and orange can each be classes.

options.text: Apple can be class 0
options.rationale: This is correct because class indices can assign apple to position 0. That position then corresponds to apple in outputs.

options.text: Orange can be class 2
options.rationale: This is correct because orange may be assigned class 2. Its target therefore uses the final position.

options.text: A target output is an image's filter kernel
options.rationale: A filter kernel is a weighted array used to extract features. A target output represents the desired class pattern for a known image.
options.better_fit: This would fit naming the weighted array applied during convolution.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Classes are possible categories, and known classes have corresponding target outputs.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: When banana is class 1, [0.0, 1.0, 0.0] is its desired target output.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The middle position represents class 1, banana.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The banana image would be compared with the wrong desired category pattern.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A target places 1.0 at the known class position and 0.0 at all other positions.

payload.prompt: A possible image category, such as apple or banana, is a _____.

parts.text: A possible image category, such as apple or banana, is a

payload.explanation: A class is a possible category the model can predict, whereas a label names the category assigned to an image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The category list would be confused with an image name, feature representation, or output function.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use class for a possible category. A label is assigned to an image, feature maps are filter outputs, and softmax produces probabilities.

payload.prompt: A smart-checkout trainer maps apple, banana, and orange to positions 0, 1, and 2. For an orange training photo, which target specification should the trainer enter?

options.text: Set only position 2 to 1.0
options.rationale: This is correct because orange is mapped to class 2. The target assigns 1.0 to the known class position and 0.0 to the others.

options.text: Set only position 0 to 1.0
options.rationale: Position 0 represents apple, not orange. This target would teach the model that the orange photo is apple.
options.better_fit: This would fit an apple training photo.

feedback.intrinsic: The orange photo would be treated as an apple during training.
feedback.instructional: Use 1.0 at the position of the photo's known class. Orange is position 2.

options.text: Set only position 1 to 1.0
options.rationale: Position 1 represents banana, not orange. This target would compare the orange photo against the wrong class.
options.better_fit: This would fit a banana training photo.

feedback.intrinsic: The orange photo would be compared with the banana category.
feedback.instructional: Map the known class to its correct position: orange is class 2, the final position.

options.text: Enter a probability distribution from the model
options.rationale: Model probabilities are predictions, while the target is the known answer supplied during training. The trainer must enter the desired class pattern for orange.
options.better_fit: This would fit recording the model's softmax output after it produces class scores.

feedback.intrinsic: The training comparison would use a guess instead of the known orange category.
feedback.instructional: Keep targets and predictions separate: targets encode the actual class, while softmax produces predicted probabilities.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Orange is class 2, so the target has 1.0 only at position 2.

payload.prompt: Which statements about CNN training are correct?

options.text: Loss measures prediction difference from actual labels
options.rationale: This is correct because loss measures the difference between predictions and actual labels. It indicates how much the model needs to improve.

options.text: Filter weights begin with random values
options.rationale: This is correct because weights begin as random numeric parameters. Training changes them to reduce loss.

options.text: Training repeats for multiple epochs
options.rationale: This is correct because an epoch is a repeat through training data. Multiple epochs allow continued weight adjustment.

options.text: Saved weights are known labels for new images
options.rationale: Saved weights are learned numeric parameters used to make predictions. They are not known labels for new images.
options.better_fit: This would fit describing learned parameters saved after training.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training starts with random weights, uses loss, and repeats across epochs.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: CNN training changes weights to increase the loss between predictions and actual labels.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training changes weights to reduce loss.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Predictions would move farther from actual categories instead of becoming more accurate.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Loss measures prediction difference, and training adjusts weights to reduce that difference.

payload.prompt: Arrange these CNN training-loop steps in order.
payload.explanation: The model predicts, compares with the actual label, calculates loss, and then adjusts weights to reduce loss.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Weights would be changed before the prediction error had been measured.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: First predict, then compare with the actual label, calculate loss, and adjust weights.

payload.prompt: The measure of difference between predicted class scores and actual labels is called _____.

parts.text: The measure of difference between predicted class scores and actual labels is called

payload.explanation: Loss measures the difference between predicted class scores and actual labels and guides weight changes.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The training loop would name a different component instead of its prediction-difference measure.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Softmax creates probabilities, feature maps represent extracted features, and classes are categories. Loss measures prediction difference.

payload.prompt: A computer-vision engineer finds poor training predictions in a fruit CNN and must improve the model before saving it. Which actions belong in the training loop?

options.text: Compare predictions with actual labels
options.rationale: This is correct because comparison supplies the information needed to measure prediction error. Actual labels provide the known answer.

options.text: Calculate the loss
options.rationale: This is correct because loss measures the difference between predictions and actual labels. It guides improvement during training.

options.text: Adjust filter and network weights
options.rationale: This is correct because training changes weights to reduce loss. Repeated adjustments improve predictions over epochs.

options.text: Replace actual labels with softmax probabilities
options.rationale: Softmax probabilities are predicted outputs, while actual labels are the known training answers. Replacing labels would remove the reference needed to calculate loss.
options.better_fit: This would fit producing predicted probabilities after class scores are created.

feedback.intrinsic: The engineer would lose the known category needed to evaluate each prediction.
feedback.instructional: Keep actual labels and predicted probabilities separate; compare them, calculate loss, and adjust weights to reduce it.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training compares predictions with actual labels, calculates loss, and adjusts weights to reduce it.
